profile.title: A laboratory profile shaped by precision, research and continuous learning.
profile.body: I hold Spanish vocational qualifications as Técnico Superior en Laboratorio Clínico y Biomédico (Higher Technician in Clinical and Biomedical Laboratory) and Técnico en Operaciones de Laboratorio (Technician in Laboratory Operations). I am currently based in the Bonn–Cologne region, with additional geographic availability in Berlin and Madrid, and I apply this training to clinical diagnostics, molecular biology, immunology and analytical laboratory work under GLP standards.

documentExplorer.description: Co-authored with Luis Gonzalo Legua Pérez · Published with co-author permission
documentExplorer.originalHypothesisFigureAlt: Conceptual diagram of the original hypothesis combining bacteriophages, chitosan, bacterial biofilms and microplastic-bacteria complex destabilization.
documentExplorer.hypothesisCaption: Simplified model: phages would target bacteria associated with biofilms, while chitosan-based materials would be studied for microplastic interaction or capture.
documentExplorer.hypothesisContribution: As an individual contribution by Jhon Michael Cuenca Jaramillo within this collaborative final project, the work proposes a future research concept combining bacteriophage specificity with chitosan-based adsorption. The hypothesis does not suggest that phages act directly on plastic polymers; instead, it explores an indirect intervention model involving microbiota, microplastic-associated biofilms and functional biomaterials.
documentExplorer.hypothesisModel: In this model, sequencing methods could help identify microorganisms with affinity for microplastic surfaces, supporting the selection or design of highly specific phages. Combined with chitosan, these phages could be studied in controlled laboratory conditions to assess whether biofilm destabilization improves microplastic interaction, capture or later analytical evaluation.
documentExplorer.hypothesisLimits: This concept is presented as an original, early-stage research hypothesis. It would require in vitro validation, toxicity assessment, reproducible analytical controls and clinical caution before any biomedical interpretation.
documentExplorer.abstractIntro: Antimicrobial resistance has renewed scientific interest in bacteriophage therapy, particularly for infections in which conventional treatments are limited.
documentExplorer.abstractReview: This co-authored final academic project is a structured literature review: 75 articles were assessed and 51 selected using explicit criteria across Spanish, English, Portuguese and Russian sources. It does not present original experimental or clinical results.
documentExplorer.abstractScope: The review explains bacteriophages, their replication cycles, potential applications, limitations, administration routes and the regulatory barriers affecting wider clinical use.
documentExplorer.abstractInterpretation: The cited literature describes promising applications and important constraints. Any discussion of specificity, microbiota effects or immune modulation reflects reviewed evidence and does not constitute clinical validation by the authors.
documentExplorer.abstractConclusion: The project also proposes a future-oriented concept connecting bacteriophages, chitosan and microplastic-associated biofilms. This contribution remains conceptual and requires separate experimental validation.
documentExplorer.keywords: Keywords: bacteriophage therapy, multidrug-resistant bacteria, phage treatment, antibiotics, alternative therapy, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

privacyPage.title: Privacy information for professional contact.
privacyPage.intro: This page explains the current data flow when the portfolio contact form is used.
privacyPage.controllerBody: Jhon M. Cuenca is responsible for the personal data submitted through this portfolio contact form. Contact is available through the professional contact form on the portfolio.
privacyPage.dataBody: The form asks for your name, email address and message. Web3Forms states that submission processing may also include technical metadata such as IP address, timestamp and referrer information. Please send only information needed for your professional enquiry.
privacyPage.purposeBody: The information is used to receive and respond to professional enquiries, laboratory opportunities, research-related contact or collaboration requests. Depending on the context, processing may be necessary for steps requested before a potential employment or other contract under Article 6(1)(b) GDPR, or may rely on the legitimate interest under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR in receiving and responding to relevant professional correspondence.
privacyPage.providerBody: The contact form is transmitted through Web3Forms, operated by Web3Creative, which acts as processor for form submissions. Web3Forms states that it operates from India, uses infrastructure including AWS, Cloudflare and Hetzner, and may process data in multiple regions. For transfers from the EEA, United Kingdom or Switzerland that require a transfer mechanism, its DPA incorporates Standard Contractual Clauses. Its current DPA also lists spam-prevention sub-processors including CleanTalk and Akismet, which may receive the submitter IP address and email address.
privacyPage.retentionBody: The static portfolio itself does not maintain a separate submissions database. Web3Forms states that form-submission data is subject to a physical time-to-live of up to three years, while dashboard visibility can depend on the plan and data may be deleted earlier. The delivered message may also remain in the receiving email service according to its settings and policies.
privacyPage.rightsBody: Where the GDPR applies, you may have rights including access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and the right to lodge a complaint with a competent data protection supervisory authority.
privacyPage.trackingBody: This portfolio does not use advertising trackers, behavioural profiling or analytics services.
